tip: 'lekker' isn't only about taste. In 'slaap lekker' it means pleasantly or well, the usual Dutch way to say good night.
For sound, 'hard' means loud, not difficult. So 'de muziek stond te hard' says the music was too loud.
Starting with 'Nergens' flips subject and verb: it becomes 'vind je', not 'je vindt', keeping the verb in second place.
'snappen van' wraps around 'er': 'ik snap er niks van' = I understand nothing of it. 'er ... van' points to the topic.
'houden' needs 'van' to mean love: 'hij hield van haar' = he loved her. Without 'van' it means to keep or hold.
'zowel ... als' pairs two items as both and: 'zowel de bus als de tram' = both the bus and the tram.
After 'dat', Dutch pushes the verbs to the end: 'dat hij de fout had gemaakt', not 'dat hij had de fout gemaakt'.
